ashley: Quick perf smoke: compared paged-fused-attn vs flash-attn-hybrid on g5. seq=2048 batch=8, kv layout=interleaved, dtype=bf16. Results surprising — fused slower.

 tj: Can you paste the profiler output? nvprof or nsight metrics help.

 ashley: paste:
```
# run: ./bench --kernel paged-fused --kv interleave --dtype bf16 --seq 2048 --batch 8
paged-fused: 31.7 ms (total kernel wall)
flash-hybrid: 18.9 ms
nvprof notes: sm_efficiency drop ~12% on kernel 'kv_gather'
extra memcpy ~1.2ms between page boundaries (observed in timeline)
```

 samir: That smells like alignment/stride causing extra page copies. Interleaved layout adds padding every 128 bytes which can trigger extra memcpy when crossing page boundaries.

 yuki: Try separate layout (keys/vals contiguous per head). We saw ~15-25% improvement for bf16 previously due to aligned 128/256-byte loads. Run with `--kv-layout separate --kv-align 256`.

 ashley: I reran: `./bench --kernel paged-fused --kv separate --kv-align 256 --dtype bf16`
```
paged-fused (separate,align256): 19.8 ms
flash-hybrid (separate): 18.7 ms
```
Looks much closer; the interleaved -> separate delta was the culprit.

 perf-bot: perf-regression alert: nightly detected +9% avg latency on paged-fused tests (suspect commit abc1234).

 tj: So paged-fused is fine once KV layout fixed. Plan: (1) add runtime stride/alignment checks and fall back to separate layout when needed, (2) add a fast path in interleaved path to avoid temporary memcpy when stride % 256 == 0, (3) add microbench to CI to catch this.

 ashley: I'll open a PR with the repro script + perf patch and assign to @samir and @yuki for review. :thumbsup:

 yuki: Also please test dtype=f16 vs bf16 and page-size sensitivity (4k vs 64k) — prefetch behavior can change perf.

 ashley: noted, adding those to the repro matrix and will post updated numbers in a follow-up thread.
